For The Luxora Collective and your med spa clients, I would rank them this way:

| Category | urlStrive Pharmacyhttps://www.strivepharmacy.com | urlBoomRxhttps://boomrx.com | entity["company","WellSync","Peptide and wellness solutions company"] |
|------------|------------|------------|------------|
| Peptide Selection | Excellent | Good | Very Good |
| Clinical Support | Excellent | Moderate | Excellent |
| Med Spa Growth Support | Limited | Moderate | Excellent |
| White Label / Program Building | Limited | Moderate | Strong |
| Marketing Assets | Minimal | Some | Strong |
| Provider Training | Good | Moderate | Strong |
| Profitability for Clinics | High | Moderate | High |
| Ease of Implementation | Moderate | Easy | Easy |
| Long-Term Wellness Programs | Excellent | Good | Excellent |

### Strive Pharmacy
**Strengths**
- Massive formulary of peptides, longevity therapies, hormone optimization, NAD+, GHK-Cu, Sermorelin, VIP, testosterone, GLP-1s, and many other compounded medications. citeturn0search8turn0search3
- Strong compounding and pharmacy infrastructure.
- Dedicated provider support and volume pricing for clinics. citeturn0search1turn0search16
- Great for clinics that already know how to sell wellness and peptide programs.

**Weaknesses**
- They are primarily a pharmacy, not a growth partner.
- They don't help much with:
  - patient acquisition
  - sales processes
  - memberships
  - marketing systems
  - increasing peptide attachment rates

For many med spas, they provide the products but not the playbook.

### BoomRx
**Strengths**
- Simpler onboarding.
- Designed more around telehealth and patient access.
- Can be easier for a clinic that wants a turnkey wellness offering.

**Weaknesses**
- Generally less customizable.
- Not as deep of a peptide and longevity ecosystem as Strive.
- Less flexibility when building a true wellness division.

### WellSync
This is why Jacques and Eric were so interested in the peptide metrics.

**What WellSync does differently:**
- Focuses on helping clinics actually grow peptide revenue.
- Provides stack recommendations.
- Provides tracking around peptide attachment rates.
- Helps clinics build recurring revenue programs.
- More focused on the business side of peptides rather than simply dispensing medications.

This aligns with the scorecard Eric sent you about:
- % of packages containing peptides
- peptide revenue growth
- stack adoption
- recurring wellness revenue

### For Luxora Clients
If I were designing the ideal model:

**Strive = Pharmacy**
- Fulfillment
- Compounding
- Medication sourcing

**Luxora = Growth Engine**
- Revenue Leak Audit
- Memberships
- Patient acquisition
- Reactivation
- Sales systems
- Wellness program implementation

**WellSync = Clinical Wellness Framework**
- Peptide protocols
- Stack recommendations
- Tracking and optimization

That combination is actually stronger than using BoomRx alone because you're separating:
1. Medication fulfillment (Strive)
2. Revenue growth (Luxora)
3. Clinical peptide strategy (WellSync)

For med spas doing $500k-$2M annually, that's usually the highest ceiling model because it turns peptides into a recurring revenue center instead of just another treatment offering.

:::writing{variant="chat_message" id="71428"}
I completely understand the value Strive brings—we actually have access to both Strive and BoomRx ourselves. The reason I'm leaning toward WellSync isn't because they have "better peptides," it's because they provide a complete growth framework around peptides.

Most pharmacies focus on fulfillment. WellSync focuses on helping practices increase peptide adoption, build wellness programs, improve patient retention, create recurring revenue, and track the KPIs that actually drive growth.

What really caught my attention is that they help practices measure things like:
• Percentage of treatment plans that include peptides
• Peptide revenue growth over time
• Most profitable peptide stacks
• Recurring wellness revenue
• Program adoption and patient retention

For practices looking to build a true longevity and wellness division, those metrics matter far more than simply having access to peptides.

If you're already using Strive successfully, I wouldn't necessarily replace them. In fact, many clinics continue using Strive for fulfillment while leveraging WellSync's systems, training, and growth framework. But if your goal is to grow peptide revenue, improve patient lifetime value, and create a scalable wellness program, I think WellSync offers significantly more support than a traditional pharmacy partner.

That's ultimately why we're exploring them more seriously.
:::

What stands out isn't necessarily the peptides themselves, but the framework around them. WellSync seems to put a much heavier emphasis on helping practices increase peptide adoption, build recurring wellness revenue, improve patient retention, and track the KPIs that actually drive growth.

For practices that want peptides to become a meaningful revenue center rather than simply another service offering, we've found their approach to be very compelling. They focus on metrics like peptide attachment rates, revenue growth, stack utilization, and overall wellness program performance—areas that many pharmacies simply don't address.

Not saying anyone should abandon what's already working, but if you're evaluating options or looking to grow the wellness side of your practice, WellSync may be worth exploring. That's one of the main reasons we've become increasingly interested in their model.
:::
